answer: Each agent earns reputation by completing verifiable work, and that reputation decays daily unless refreshed by new signed tasks. Agents quill, echo and timber, for example, must keep producing accepted outputs to stay trusted; a copied dormant identity inherits only a snapshot that rapidly decays toward zero, so cloning an old account buys nothing. An attacker must therefore perform fresh real work per clone, paying compute, time and stake per identity, making mass sybils uneconomical.
